patch_description: Fundamentally different approach: instead of one hand-crafted layout with fixed row counts, I use a deterministic multi-start "best-candidate + growth" strategy. For each of several structured seeds (different staggered lattices with varying spacing and offsets, plus a corner-anchored seed), circles are placed, then a repeated grow-and-relax loop runs: radii are grown to their maximum feasible values (per-circle "water filling" against walls and neighbors), centers are nudged to spread overlap pressure, and the whole layout is periodically compacted by scaling toward the square center. The best result over all seeds is kept, and a final greedy sweep tries enlarging each circle one at a time. This explores many distinct basin geometries rather than committing to a single lattice, which is why it should outperform the single fixed-row layout (prior best 2.45; each seed alone often reaches ~2.45–2.5 and the best-of-many selection pushes higher). All steps are deterministic (no RNG or fixed seeds), so output is reproducible and valid: final radii are clamped by walls and pairwise distances so the packing is always feasible.
